{"Implementation approach":"Preserve protocol files exactly: requirements.txt, Main.py, and tests/test_main.py. Keep Main.py thin and deterministic: construct a CaroGame, execute the exact nine-move canonical sequence, print once, and exit. Place reusable, pure domain logic under a lowercase snake_case package named 'caro'. Maintain an acyclic import graph: foundational types and errors must not import engines or entrypoints; rules remain pure and separate; the engine (CaroGame) orchestrates board updates and state transitions. Python 3.10 conventions only. Tests remain headless and deterministic: they import the package and Main.py, verify core behaviors (validation precedence, canonical nine-move horizontal win, reset behavior, and error paths) using pytest and explicit exception imports, without any UI or I/O dependencies.","Domain Decomposition":[["Runtime bootstrap executing the canonical nine-move demo and printing once","Main.py","protocol-required"],["Package initialization exporting the public API only","caro/__init__.py","package"],["Foundational error types for invalid move and game-over","caro/errors.py","domain-entity"],["Enumerations for Player (X/O) and Status (IN_PROGRESS, X_WON, O_WON, DRAW)","caro/types.py","domain-entity"],["Move history entry capturing row, col, and player","caro/move.py","domain-entity"],["Board representation and operations (15x15 grid, occupancy, bounds, full-check)","caro/board.py","domain-entity"],["Pure win detection rule has_five_or_more across four principal directions","caro/rules.py","pure-rule"],["CaroGame engine orchestrating turns, validation precedence, state transitions, and reset","caro/game.py","orchestration"],["Protocol-level pytest verifying runtime wiring and core rules","tests/test_main.py","automated-test"]],"File list":["requirements.txt","Main.py","caro/__init__.py","caro/errors.py","caro/types.py","caro/move.py","caro/board.py","caro/rules.py","caro/game.py","tests/test_main.py"],"Canonical File References":["requirements.txt","Main.py","caro/__init__.py","caro/errors.py","caro/types.py","caro/move.py","caro/board.py","caro/rules.py","caro/game.py","tests/test_main.py"],"Data structures and interfaces":"classDiagram
    class CaroGame {
        -Board _board
        -Player _current_player
        -Player _first_player
        -Status _status
        -Player~nullable~ _winner
        -list~Move~ _history
        +__init__(size: int = 15, first_player: Player = Player.X)
        +move(row: int, col: int)
        +reset()
        +board() list~list~Player|None~~
        +current_player() Player
        +status() Status
        +winner() Player|None
        +history() list~Move~
    }

    class Board {
        -int size
        -list~list~Player|None~~ grid
        +__init__(size: int = 15)
        +get_cell(row: int, col: int) Player|None
        +set_cell(row: int, col: int, player: Player)
        +in_bounds(row: int, col: int) bool
        +is_empty(row: int, col: int) bool
        +is_full() bool
        +to_matrix() list~list~Player|None~~
    }

    class Move {
        +row: int
        +col: int
        +player: Player
    }

    class Player {
        <<enum>>
        X
        O
    }

    class Status {
        <<enum>>
        IN_PROGRESS
        X_WON
        O_WON
        DRAW
    }

    class Rules {
        <<function>> has_five_or_more(board: Board, row: int, col: int, player: Player) bool
    }

    class InvalidMoveError
    class GameOverError

    CaroGame --> Board
    CaroGame ..> Move
    CaroGame ..> Player
    CaroGame ..> Status
    CaroGame ..> Rules : uses
    CaroGame ..> InvalidMoveError
    CaroGame ..> GameOverError
    Rules ..> Board
    Rules ..> Player","Program call flow":"sequenceDiagram
    participant M as Main.py
    participant G as CaroGame
    participant B as Board
    participant R as Rules
    M->>G: construct(size=15, first_player=X)
    loop Canonical nine-move sequence
        M->>G: move(row,col)
        G->>G: validate status IN_PROGRESS else raise GameOverError
        G->>B: in_bounds(row,col)? else InvalidMoveError
        G->>B: is_empty(row,col)? else InvalidMoveError
        G->>B: set_cell(row,col,current_player)
        G->>R: has_five_or_more(B,row,col,current_player)?
        alt win
            G->>G: set status to X_WON/O_WON; set winner; do not toggle
        else no win
            G->>B: is_full()? draw if true
            G->>G: toggle player if still IN_PROGRESS
        end
    end
    M->>M: print single status line and exit","Domain Mapping":[["Public API surface (CaroGame, Player, Status, Move, errors exports)","caro/__init__.py"],["Error signaling for invalid moves and post-game attempts","caro/errors.py"],["Player and Status enumerations","caro/types.py"],["Move history entries","caro/move.py"],["15x15 board storage, bounds and occupancy helpers, full detection","caro/board.py"],["Pure win detection function has_five_or_more across four directions","caro/rules.py"],["CaroGame engine: move validation precedence, turn handling, win/draw detection, history, reset","caro/game.py"],["Thin runtime demo performing the exact nine moves and printing once","Main.py"],["Automated tests covering runtime wiring, canonical win, validation precedence, reset, and GameOverError","tests/test_main.py"]],"Testable Core Boundary":{"pure_logic_modules":["caro/__init__.py","caro/errors.py","caro/types.py","caro/move.py","caro/board.py","caro/rules.py","caro/game.py"],"environment_dependent_modules":["Main.py"],"test_targets_should_focus_on":["Runtime wiring via Main.run_demo() returns a terminal game with X win after nine moves","Validation precedence: GameOverError before any other checks; Module: caro.errors
- class InvalidMoveError(Exception): raised when a move is invalid while the game is IN_PROGRESS (e.g., out-of-bounds or cell occupied). Message must be informative but tests rely only on type.
- class GameOverError(Exception): raised when attempting to move after the game has ended (win or draw). Tests rely on type.

Module: caro.types
- enum Player(Enum): X = 'X', O = 'O'. Stable identity and string representation not relied upon beyond enum equality.
- enum Status(Enum): IN_PROGRESS = 'IN_PROGRESS', X_WON = 'X_WON', O_WON = 'O_WON', DRAW = 'DRAW'.

Module: caro.move
- @dataclass(frozen=True) class Move: row: int; col: int; player: Player. Immutable record appended to game history per successful move.

Module: caro.board
- class Board:
  - __init__(self, size: int = 15): initialize square grid size x size with None cells; size must be >= 1.
  - in_bounds(self, row: int, col: int) -> bool: returns True if 0 <= row < size and 0 <= col < size.
  - get_cell(self, row: int, col: int) -> Player | None: returns occupant or None; requires in-bounds; callers ensure bounds.
  - is_empty(self, row: int, col: int) -> bool: True if cell is None; requires in-bounds.
  - set_cell(self, row: int, col: int, player: Player) -> None: sets cell to player; requires in-bounds and empty; engine enforces validations.
  - is_full(self) -> bool: True if no None cells remain.
  - to_matrix(self) -> list[list[Player | None]]: deep copy of grid for external observation.

Module: caro.rules
- def has_five_or_more(board: Board, row: int, col: int, player: Player) -> bool: Pure function; checks if placing player at (row, col) creates a contiguous line of length >= 5 in any of four directions: horizontal (0,1), vertical (1,0), diagonal down-right (1,1), diagonal up-right (-1,1). Counts include the placed stone; reads board via get_cell and in_bounds only; no mutations or side effects.

Module: caro.game
- class CaroGame:
  - __init__(self, size: int = 15, first_player: Player = Player.X): creates Board(size), sets _first_player and _current_player, sets _status = Status.IN_PROGRESS, _winner = None, and empty _history.
  - move(self, row: int, col: int) -> None: Validation order strictly enforced:
    1) If status != IN_PROGRESS: raise GameOverError before any other check; history/state unchanged.
    2) If not board.in_bounds(row, col): raise InvalidMoveError.
    3) If not board.is_empty(row, col): raise InvalidMoveError.
    On success: board.set_cell(row, col, _current_player), append Move(row, col, _current_player) to history; call rules.has_five_or_more; if True, set status to X_WON/O_WON accordingly, set _winner, and do not toggle player. Else, if board.is_full(): set status to DRAW; else toggle _current_player and leave status IN_PROGRESS.
  - reset(self) -> None: reset board to empty, clear history, set status to IN_PROGRESS, set winner None, and restore _current_player to _first_player.
  - board(self) -> list[list[Player | None]]: return Board.to_matrix() snapshot.
  - current_player(self) -> Player: return current active player.
  - status(self) -> Status: return current game status.
  - winner(self) -> Player | None: return winner when status is X_WON or O_WON; else None.
  - history(self) -> list[Move]: return a shallow copy or read-only view of history (tests will not mutate).

Module: caro.__init__
- Export symbols: CaroGame, Player, Status, Move, InvalidMoveError, GameOverError; do not execute code at import time beyond symbol binding.

Module: Main
- Behavior: Construct CaroGame(size=15, first_player=Player.X); execute the exact canonical nine-move sequence to achieve a horizontal X win on the ninth move; print a single status line (e.g., 'Status: X_WON') and exit. No loops beyond fixed sequence, no input, no randomness.

Import direction constraints
- caro/errors.py and caro/types.py are foundational and must not import from caro.game, caro.rules, or Main.
- caro/rules.py imports only Board and Player (from caro.board and caro.types). It must not import CaroGame or Main.
- caro/game.py may import Board, Move, Player, Status, and errors, as well as rules.has_five_or_more.
- Main.py imports only from caro package; tests import Main and caro.* modules only.","Shared Knowledge":"The project preserves protocol files requirements.txt, Main.py, and tests/test_main.py. The public API is exposed via caro/__init__.py and includes CaroGame, Player, Status, Move, InvalidMoveError, and GameOverError. The import graph is acyclic: errors/types/move/board are foundational, rules is pure, and game orchestrates. Main.py is a thin, deterministic bootstrap that constructs CaroGame, performs exactly nine moves, prints once, and exits. Tests are headless and deterministic; they import Main, caro, caro.errors, and caro.types only; no UI or I/O interactions beyond a single print in Main.py.","Execution Protocol":"Run tests with: python -m pytest -q. There is exactly one protocol-level test file: tests/test_main.py. Runtime entrypoint is Main.py, which executes a canonical nine-move demo, prints a single status line, and exits. No manual interaction, network, or OS-dependent behavior is permitted. Additional files must not alter protocol files.","Anything UNCLEAR":"Default board size is assumed to be 15 (consistent with the design). If a different default size is required for the canonical coordinates, please confirm."}
